groups.directions:
Topic: Sentence Improvement
Subtopic: Grammar Improvement

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: The committee have decided to unanimously reject the highly controversial proposal submitted by the urban development board last week.

options.label: A
options.text: The committee has decided to unanimously reject the highly controversial proposal

options.label: B
options.text: The committee have decided unanimously rejecting the highly controversial proposal

options.label: C
options.text: The committee has decide to unanimously reject the highly controversial proposal

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: "Committee" is a collective noun. The word "unanimously" indicates they are acting as a single, undivided unit. Therefore, it must take the singular verb "has decided".

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: No sooner he had entered the dimly lit room than the heavy oak door slammed shut behind him.

options.label: A
options.text: No sooner did he entered the dimly lit room than

options.label: B
options.text: No sooner had he entered the dimly lit room than

options.label: C
options.text: No sooner he entered the dimly lit room when

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with "No sooner", it requires an inverted word order (auxiliary verb before the subject). "No sooner had he entered" is the correct grammatical structure.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: I would have definitely helped you complete the assignment if you would have asked me earlier.

options.label: A
options.text: if you had asked me earlier.

options.label: B
options.text: if you have asked me earlier.

options.label: C
options.text: if you asked me earlier.

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: In a third conditional sentence (unreal past), the "if" clause must be in the past perfect tense ("if you had asked"), while the main clause uses "would have + past participle". "If you would have" is a common but incorrect phrasing.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: One of the most significant challenge faced by the developing nation is the severe lack of clean drinking water.

options.label: A
options.text: One of the most significant challenges faced by the developing nation are

options.label: B
options.text: One of the most significant challenges faced by the developing nation is

options.label: C
options.text: One of the most significant challenge faced by the developing nations is

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: The phrase "One of the" is always followed by a plural noun ("challenges"), but because the actual subject is "One", the main verb must be singular ("is").

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: Despite of his immense wealth and global influence, the eccentric billionaire lived a remarkably solitary and miserable life.

options.label: A
options.text: In spite his immense wealth and global influence,

options.label: B
options.text: Despite his immense wealth and global influence,

options.label: C
options.text: Although of his immense wealth and global influence,

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: The preposition "despite" takes a noun or gerund directly without the preposition "of". ("In spite of" is correct, but "Despite of" is always wrong).

groups.directions:
Topic: Sentence Improvement
Subtopic: Grammar Improvement

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: The brilliant scientist, along with her entire team of researchers, were honored at the international gala.

options.label: A
options.text: along with her entire team of researchers, are honored

options.label: B
options.text: along with her entire team of researchers, was honored

options.label: C
options.text: along with her entire team of researchers, have been honored

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: When subjects are connected by phrases like "along with", the verb must agree with the first subject ("The brilliant scientist", which is singular). Therefore, "was honored" is correct.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: Having finished the incredibly complex project, the manager allowed the exhausted team to leave early.

options.label: A
options.text: Having finish the incredibly complex project,

options.label: B
options.text: Have finished the incredibly complex project,

options.label: C
options.text: After having finished the incredibly complex project,

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: "Having finished" is a perfect participle correctly indicating an action completed before the main verb's action. The sentence is grammatically flawless as written.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: He is not only an exceptionally talented musician but also plays tennis at a professional level.

options.label: A
options.text: Not only is he an exceptionally talented musician but he also plays tennis

options.label: B
options.text: He not only is an exceptionally talented musician but also plays tennis

options.label: C
options.text: He is not only an exceptionally talented musician but also a professional tennis player.

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: Correlative conjunctions like "not only... but also" require parallel structure. In the original, "an exceptionally talented musician" (a noun phrase) is paired with "plays tennis" (a verb phrase). Option C perfectly balances two noun phrases.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: The number of cyberattacks targeting financial institutions have increased exponentially over the last decade.

options.label: A
options.text: A number of cyberattacks targeting financial institutions has increased

options.label: B
options.text: The number of cyberattacks targeting financial institutions has increased

options.label: C
options.text: The numbers of cyberattacks targeting financial institutions have increased

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: The phrase "The number of" (referring to a specific mathematical quantity) always takes a singular verb ("has increased"), unlike "A number of", which takes a plural verb.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: Unless you do not apologize for your highly unprofessional behavior, the board will terminate your contract immediately.

options.label: A
options.text: Unless you will not apologize for your highly unprofessional behavior,

options.label: B
options.text: If you do not apologize for your highly unprofessional behavior,

options.label: C
options.text: Unless you apologize for your highly unprofessional behavior,

options.label: D
options.text: Both B and C are correct improvements.

questions.explanation: "Unless" inherently means "if not", so it cannot be followed by a negative word like "not" ("Unless you do not" is a double negative). Both "If you do not apologize" and "Unless you apologize" are grammatically correct and convey the identical meaning.

groups.directions:
Topic: Sentence Improvement
Subtopic: Grammar Improvement

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: The intricate details of the historical treaty is not fully understood by most modern political analysts.

options.label: A
options.text: The intricate details of the historical treaty are not fully understood

options.label: B
options.text: The intricate detail of the historical treaty are not fully understood

options.label: C
options.text: The intricate details of the historical treaty has not fully understood

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: The true subject of the sentence is "details" (plural). "Of the historical treaty" is just a prepositional phrase modifying the subject. Therefore, the plural verb "are" must be used.

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: I look forward to meet you at the upcoming global technology summit in San Francisco.

options.label: A
options.text: I look forward to have met you at

options.label: B
options.text: I look forward to meeting you at

options.label: C
options.text: I am looking forward to meet you at

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: The phrase "look forward to" ends with a preposition ("to"), so the verb following it must be in the gerund form ("meeting").

questions.text:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence that improves upon the original.
Original: The newly constructed bridge is much more stronger than the older one that collapsed last year.

options.label: A
options.text: is much stronger than the older one

options.label: B
options.text: is more stronger than the older one

options.label: C
options.text: is much more strong than the older one

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

options.label: A
options.text: Neither the employees nor the department manager has been informed

options.label: B
options.text: Neither the employee nor the department managers has been informed

options.label: C
options.text: Neither the employees or the department manager have been informed

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

options.label: A
options.text: takes strictly action against

options.label: B
options.text: took strict action against

options.label: C
options.text: will take strict action against

options.label: D
options.text: The original sentence is correct.

questions.explanation: "Stronger" is already in the comparative degree. Using "more" with it creates an incorrect double comparative ("more stronger"). "Much" can correctly modify a comparative ("much stronger").
